The paper also gives a quantitative route using ten timelike observers with matched bulk, area and stationarity errors o(ℓ⁴); it requires no separately assumed null-balance equation.

criteria.title: Lorentzian event and geometry domain
criteria.requires: On one candidate-generated refinement tower supply an authenticated causal order, event placement and count/volume limits that agree on a local differentiable, stably causal Lorentzian domain.
criteria.note: Scalar propagation and native local clock counts are available, but a joint transferred angular/radial state and causal-volume refinement tower are missing.

criteria.title: Cap modular charges measure the propagating matter stress
criteria.requires: Calibrate cap modular flow to geometric normalization and show its directional charges measure the same stress tensor that the candidate uses in propagation and interactions.
criteria.note: A local cage frequency and a source-energy ledger are measured. Their identification with geometrically normalized cap charges remains open.

criteria.title: Independent matter Ward identity
criteria.requires: Derive or test a covariantly conserved matter stress tensor on the G1 domain, using matter dynamics independently of the Einstein equation.
criteria.note: Finite source/work accounting has no covariant stress-divergence identity on a matched geometry.

criteria.title: Stationary generalized entropy at fixed proper volume
criteria.requires: For the same region and state establish the edge-center entropy split and physical area normalization, modular first law, and vanishing first variation of generalized entropy at fixed proper volume.
criteria.note: The scalar source and its retained pointer histories supply no measured edge-center split and matched fixed-volume variation.

criteria.title: Small-ball control and sufficient null directions
criteria.requires: Bound the small-ball remainders across scales and demonstrate enough independent observer and null directions to recover directional tensor data in the same regional frame.
criteria.note: Local source and fuel measurements supply no shrinking-ball frame, angular tomography or uniform error estimate.

criteria.title: Universal coupling and a shared positive Newton constant
criteria.requires: Use a common vacuum and calibration. Establish that all admitted excitations couple to the same responsive geometry with one positive Newton constant.
criteria.note: The native scalar sector has no implemented universally coupled responsive geometry.

criteria.title: Null balance and tensor closure
criteria.requires: For the same source, state, tower and calibrated coupling, compare G(k,k) with 8πG times the measured T(k,k) on all nine spanning null design directions, control the residual, then apply independent Ward and geometric Bianchi identities to fix the remaining trace up to Λ.
criteria.note: No matched native curvature/stress experiment is present. The static radial counterexample in the spacetime paper belongs to a separately specified construction.

requirements.title: Clock dilation, three-dimensional fields, signal timing and bound-pair dynamics
requirements.purpose: Observers measure how a moving clock runs, whether a field varies along three independent spatial directions, and when a message can first be decoded. They also test whether separated loads form a lasting pair, where it travels and whether it returns, how its clock phase advances, and how its wave frequency depends on momentum.
requirements.reference: The archived positive and negative controls ran on an eight-slot periodic routing architecture. The historical numbers belong to that apparatus. The candidate columns use the current spherical law and state which preparations, sectors and services produced their records.

criteria.title: Time dilation of a moving clock
criteria.requires: Measure speed independently. Read a returning finite patch’s evolving hand and its rest companion at home. Reproduce the clock forecast and its tolerance on held journeys, clock constructions and speeds.
criteria.context: On the torus five long-wave moving/rest residuals were at most 0.00371 against a 0.035 limit. A broad packet missed by 0.06546. Two clocks agreed on five journeys. Six bound-clock flights passed the finite-packet correction.
criteria.note: A stationary ring has a measurable line against its reference. A transported clock, independent speed and fixed-home reunion remain open.

criteria.title: Three spatial directions in a field measured by observers
criteria.requires: Infer three independent directions and scales from timed patch records. Predict withheld field measurements across stations and refinements and test whether dropping any direction spoils them.
criteria.context: The torus supplied its three spatial routing axes. Nine stations predicted 120 held field values with RMS 0.001103. Omitting successive spatial derivatives raised RMS to 0.3123, 0.3246 and 0.3246. RER also recovered a three-dimensional Gram matrix from native cell records and, in a separate free-field inverse experiment, a supplied cube from eight relabelled channels.
criteria.note: The seam response BBᵀ has a three-dimensional first nonconstant eigenspace on one cell. The registered scalar generator supplies cell modes. A propagation experiment with independently surveyed stations remains open.

criteria.title: Earliest decodable message in observer time
criteria.requires: Choose a bit after setup. The receiver commits its answer by independently ranged early and late deadlines on its own patch clock. Test passive signals, every allowed relay and quiet controls. Record both accuracy and rare early clicks.
criteria.context: The torus passive receiver had early probability at most 5.878 × 10⁻³⁵, early balanced decoding at 50% and late decoding at 100%. An addressed relay decoded all 512 bits early. A pulse peak measures a different event from the first usable message.
criteria.note: The scalar service prepares and reads local pointer signals. Its protocol does not compare early and late remote decoding on observers’ clocks.

criteria.title: Formation of an enduring pair in an ordinary encounter
criteria.requires: Start with separated constituents. A patch records a birth and later an intact pair. Distinguish formation from binding after a measurement or deliberate preparation, report all quiet starts and compare disabled capture.
criteria.context: The archived simple routed encounter formed a pair with probability 1/2 and gave zero when its capture vertex was disabled. Preparation and capture rates depend on the experiment.
criteria.note: The pulse prepares the protected ring. The registered free scalar generator has no interaction term that binds two colliding objects. The separate conversion experiment changes the law.

criteria.title: Direction, coverage and return of a formed pair
criteria.requires: Register direction by the time order of local station records. Report intended and wrong-way crossings per enrolled start and per crossing for both launch senses. Read the marker and pair at return and include losses.
criteria.context: The archived late train reached 96.56% in the intended direction among crossings. Early coverage was 9.680% against 10% required. The closed-wire example had about 0.53% breakup after its marker’s second return.
criteria.note: The observed ring is exactly confined. The free scalar response has other modes, but the specified direction-and-return experiment has no registered formed-pair cohort.

criteria.title: Phase rate of a clock on the formed pair
criteria.requires: Read the same internal phase at several declared elapsed intervals using local reference records. Include visibility, rate uncertainty, source width, receiver aperture and quiet outcomes.
criteria.context: At width five the torus array reported 0.000439509–0.000440033 radians per home tick across six durations. The central layer failed. Widening the preparation from three to five changed the array rate by about 31%.
criteria.note: A pulsed cage gives 4.898982 and 4.898976 in local reference units under equal and unequal waits. A fuel read gives 4.898980. This is a stationary prepared cage with a supplied phase.

criteria.title: Relativistic matter-wave dispersion of the same formed object
criteria.requires: Independently measure rest frequency, signal speed and spatial phase gradient. Predict the moving object’s frequency in held directions and at multiple wavelengths with a changed-law control.
criteria.context: The archived routed pair passed 14 signed directions at periods 64, 128 and 256, with a 3.5% kinetic tolerance. Halving the spatial weight failed all 42 comparisons. The higher-momentum runs left the smooth regime.
criteria.note: The seam operator has the exact spectral relation ω² = m² + λ. Here λ comes from BBᵀ and m is supplied. The cage measures one internal gap. An observer-derived wavevector, independent signal speed and held moving-pair shell are open.

requirements.title: Patch clocks, stable excitations and a spacetime description
requirements.purpose: Record what the spherical candidates have already demonstrated at finite size and which ingredients a full spacetime reconstruction still needs.
requirements.reference: A patch can own one or several echosahedra and may share cells with another observer. Supplied references, detectors and local schedules belong to each experiment. A source comparison may use an unchanged reducing sector when the preparation, generator and readout coincide.

criteria.title: A fixed observer reads a material timing record
criteria.requires: A finite patch reads a local hand or periodic reference from physical registers at more than one setting. State how the source, cadence and readout are supplied.
criteria.context: This finite test credits a readable clock resource with its preparation and range. A universal clock rate or a shared screen-wide history is outside its scope.
criteria.note: A native cell’s ring detector and a prepared local reference yield a single phase line after a finite pulse. Stopping both cage modes removes the swing while its reference continues.

criteria.title: Own-history clock transport and fixed-home reunion
criteria.requires: A finite moving patch physically carries its hand, elapsed count and interval history. At reunion both owners recover the same home/traveller readings through a shared local register. State all supplied movement and gating services.
criteria.context: This measures local register custody and agreement at one event. A distribution over completed travel schedules also tests the closing filter over its declared finite capacity.
criteria.note: The cage phase can be read locally. It is fixed to the ring. The routed scratch service transports a control, with no moving cage hand or joint reunion record.

criteria.title: A prepared excitation persists and is locally detectable
criteria.requires: Give a fixed preparation, a patch readout, delays and a perturbation or interaction-off control. Demonstrate persistence of internal binding or protected local support and specify which is tested.
criteria.context: Later torus work added persistence as an eighth observation. Survival of a prepared state is independently testable and does not imply that the same state forms in a typical encounter.
criteria.note: The alternating four-seam ring and its partner span an invariant subspace. The detector reads the excitation over five waits. Altering the hopping breaks the line and its predicted records. Ring tests cover 20, 80 and 320 cells.

criteria.title: Propagation of a localized defect or bound excitation
criteria.requires: After a local excitation is identified, another local site or patch detects it with its identifying property intact. Specify whether transport is passive or serviced and keep disappearance and quiet outcomes.
criteria.context: Motion of a bound pair to another seam, transport of a registered load between patches and motion of a phase-carrying particle are distinct measurements. Only the first two meet this bounded location-change test.
criteria.note: The measured cage has exactly flat levels and remains confined to its ring. A separately named mobile-memory generator changes the dynamics. A mobile protected scalar excitation in the registered law remains open.

criteria.title: Smooth 3+1D description of a finite observer menu
criteria.requires: On the same candidate identify the recorded source, clock, positive angular form, radial propagation and refinement assumptions of the smooth-description proposition, or directly verify a declared family of held four-dimensional predictions with quantified errors.
criteria.context: RER’s smooth-effective-descriptions proposition proves approximation of every fixed finite admissible menu on bounded times by a free scalar on a smooth static 1+3 metric under S1 and S2 with radial Dirichlet interval. An earlier eight-channel free-field reconstruction inferred 12 cube edges and rank three, and predicted 16 withheld settings below 3 × 10⁻¹⁴ in probability. A separate 720-branch echosahedral experiment recovered a rank-three Gram matrix from repair records. In the separate 1+3 fresh-seed signature replication the high-carrier arm recovered its threshold signature in 5/5 replicates and the lower arm in 2/5. The margin and ancestry controls failed. The small eigenvalue was about 3 × 10⁻⁵ relative to the largest and the robust signature lost a direction.
criteria.note: The free scalar law gives a native one-cell seam dispersion and a local phase reference. A source-to-metric map with radial propagation and clocked refinements over this law’s observer records remains open.

criteria.title: Three independent spatial response components in local patch records
criteria.requires: Infer the multiplicity and Gram matrix of the slowest nonconstant response from records of an observer with a finite spatial aperture. Predict new local readouts and bound the loss from a two-component description.
criteria.context: The source supplies one native cell, sharp preparations, complete local detectors, the weak-exposure branch and relative dwell settings. The inverse receives relabelled probabilities and a uniform-hopping model class. It receives no coordinates, spatial dimension, seams or Hamiltonian. The measurement concerns the local angular response. OBS-02 asks whether three directions propagate between observers.
criteria.note: The unsigned seam–port incidence sends the same rank-three projector into the actual scalar squared-frequency response. A detector-table reconstruction of that rank on physical scalar preparations remains open.

criteria.title: Three spatial response components reach neighbouring patches
criteria.requires: Use native evolution to transmit independently prepared components from one sender to real neighbouring patches. Decode held combinations from local port/quiet counts, test rank-two and sham controls, and check predictions at untrained stations or exposure times.
criteria.context: This section tests the transfer of prepared local load-probability contrasts on a one-load source. The exposures are externally set. The three receivers contribute separate local inboxes.
criteria.note: The scalar sector uses different registers and propagation. This receiver experiment has no scalar-channel counterpart.

criteria.title: Two kinds of material hand agree on the same accepted repair events
criteria.requires: Compare a transported oscillator with a registered event hand on the same guided journeys and local accepted repair histories. Use independent phase readout, a frozen equivalence margin, rest calibration and a distinct raw-event control.
criteria.context: The accepted-event oscillator and event hand implement distinct transducers of a common tick stream. The alternative oscillator counts every positive primary. Their comparison isolates the physical event selection.
criteria.note: The stationary cage line has no corresponding guided two-hand replication.

criteria.title: Optically ranged reunion on held native links and motion schedules
criteria.requires: A finite home patch measures a reciprocal light time, receives a physical arrival report and reads both elapsed words at reunion. Compare the optical forecast with the material hand for prospectively held schedules on different native links. Require all in-domain tests to meet their frozen uncertainty band, and report overflow and raw-event controls separately.
criteria.context: The relative pace of the reciprocal light guide and transfer opportunities is provided. Physical link installations with identical service timelines share their statistical cohort.
criteria.note: A held reciprocal optical comparison of the transported scalar oscillator is open.

criteria.title: Excess gravity predicted from retained patch records
criteria.requires: Specify the cut charge and its fluctuations on physical observer records. Use the gravitational response calibrated on ordinary matter to predict excess orbital and lensing signals on independent galaxies with one source law, geometry and uncertainty model.
criteria.context: This compares the macroscopic observer measurements attributed to non-luminous gravity. OW-19 assesses a stable neutral massive state.
criteria.note: The scalar channel has no registered collar-to-gravity calibration.

requirements.title: OpenWave empirical criteria
requirements.purpose: Assess the 31 OpenWave physical targets locally on every registered RER law. The public M10 column at the cited revision pins Interval Echo. OpenWave partially validated Row 4 and marked the other 30 rows as not yet tested. Each RER grade describes the measurement and scope named in its entry.

criteria.title: Charge quantization
criteria.requires: Exhibit an integer topological electric charge and exclude division of one unit between two half-charged excitations.
criteria.note: Electric topological charge and a forbidden splitting channel have yet to be identified.

criteria.title: Electron rest energy (mass)
criteria.requires: Select a localized state dynamically. With its energy anchored at 511 keV, predict and independently measure another physical quantity fixed by that anchor.
criteria.note: A prepared four-seam branch has a measured single-addition gap. Two separated additions give the sum in joint phase records. The 511 keV anchor alone supplies a scale. An independent electron observable and identification remain open.

criteria.title: de Broglie clock (Zitterbewegung)
criteria.requires: Measure an internally initiated, frequency-rigid oscillation whose angular frequency equals the measured rest energy divided by ℏ.
criteria.note: After a finite preparation pulse two local clocks resolve a free line at about 4.89898, agreeing with a separate fuel-gap measurement. Autonomous onset and the electron rest-energy identification remain open.

criteria.title: Particle stability (Derrick escape)
criteria.requires: Release the prepared particle state and measure its persistence under free evolution. Identify the excitation and the domain of the measurement. The separate SM-e entry assesses its identification as an electron.
criteria.note: With the registered cage preparation and terminal reader on one cell, the four-seam excitation persists at five free waits. Its invariant subspace keeps it localized for all times under the scalar channel's free generator.

criteria.title: Magnetic moment μ (g ≈ 2, magnetostatics)
criteria.requires: Measure a static magnetic dipole sourced by internal circulation in the stationary electron, its gyromagnetic factor near two and its Larmor response.
criteria.note: The electron dipole, gyromagnetic factor and field-driven precession require an electromagnetic readout.

criteria.title: Angular momentum J (spin ℏ/2)
criteria.requires: Measure angular momentum of magnitude ℏ/2 carried by the field of the same electron state.
criteria.note: Field angular momentum has yet to be measured on an identified electron.

criteria.title: Spin-½ statistics (720° double cover)
criteria.requires: Interfere a full rotation, or a two-core exchange, with a reference and recover a minus sign. A dynamically selected half-turn discriminated from a polar control provides intermediate evidence.
criteria.note: The scalar register construction uses fermionic operators. An interference measurement of a dynamically selected two-core exchange or 2π rotation remains open.

criteria.title: Antimatter + annihilation
criteria.requires: Observe a particle and its conjugate convert into radiation. Resolve the two- and three-photon positronium channels as follow-up measurements.
criteria.note: Local instruments distinguish adding and removing an object from the filled reference. The sharp cage occupations persist during free evolution. A radiative annihilation channel requires different evidence.

criteria.title: Neutrinos (neutral states)
criteria.requires: Identify electrically neutral, light excitations among the products of a decay.
criteria.note: The scalar law supports neutral excitations relative to its supplied gauge reference. A light neutral product released in a weak decay remains unidentified.

criteria.title: Neutrino oscillations (PMNS)
criteria.requires: Distinguish three neutrino flavours through production and detection, observe their oscillations and extract the PMNS angles.
criteria.note: The resolved bands belong to one scalar channel. Three flavour-labelled channels, their oscillations and mixing angles remain open.

criteria.title: Lepton mass spectrum (μ, τ)
criteria.requires: Resolve precisely three charged-lepton minima and compare their relative masses with 1, 207 and 3477.
criteria.note: Several scalar lines have measured frequencies for a supplied level parameter. A charged-lepton family assignment and three mass ratios remain open.

criteria.title: Quarks
criteria.requires: Recover fractional electric charge from a partial winding of a quark string.
criteria.note: An electric response tied to fractional string winding remains unmeasured.

criteria.title: Baryons: bound state (p, n)
criteria.requires: Recover a persistent bound composite whose three constituents are identified as quarks.
criteria.note: A three-quark identification remains open.

criteria.title: Baryons: mass ordering + charge profile
criteria.requires: Distinguish neutron and proton, obtain a heavier neutron and resolve the positive-core and negative-shell charge distribution.
criteria.note: The neutron and proton identities, mass order and resolved electric profile remain open.

criteria.title: Baryons: exact masses
criteria.requires: Predict the proton and neutron rest energies from the field and compare with 938.3 and 939.6 MeV, respectively.
criteria.note: A common field-based prediction for both identified baryon energies remains open.

criteria.title: Deuteron (binding + quadrupole)
criteria.requires: Demonstrate deuteron binding below the sum of the proton and neutron masses and measure its electric quadrupole.
criteria.note: No deuteron binding and electric quadrupole measurement exists on the identified constituents.

criteria.title: Nuclear structure (levels, halos)
criteria.requires: Recover nuclear binding across species, excitation levels and lifetimes of halo nuclei.
criteria.note: Identified nuclear species with binding, spectroscopy and halo lifetime records remain open.

criteria.title: Mesons (π, K)
criteria.requires: Identify pion and kaon states and a strange decay such as Λ⁰ → p + π⁻.
criteria.note: Meson assignments and a decay tagged by strangeness remain open.

criteria.title: Dark matter candidate
criteria.requires: Demonstrate a stable massive excitation with measured neutrality as a dark-matter candidate.
criteria.note: The prepared four-seam state is persistent. Its dark-matter identification requires electric neutrality and a moving inertial-mass measurement on the same branch.

criteria.title: Electric force (Coulomb 1/r, electrostatics)
criteria.requires: Measure an inverse-distance far-field potential sourced by one elementary electric charge. A strength claim also needs α derived from the mechanism.
criteria.note: The elementary free scalar law is quadratic. Green kernels of the seam operator alone establish no charged far-field potential measured by a unit source and a test object.

criteria.title: Lorentz covariance (+ Coulomb = EM)
criteria.requires: Establish Lorentz covariance without a preferred inertial frame, including contraction of boosted states and an operational signal-speed bound.
criteria.note: Four one-cell wave bands follow a relativistic scalar dispersion. The continuous-duration equal-term test has influence at arbitrarily early times. Native boosts, contraction and a finite operational signal-speed bound on the sphere remain open.

criteria.title: Strong force: confinement
criteria.requires: Measure a linear confining potential between identified colour charges and recover a string tension near 1 GeV/fm.
criteria.note: A colour-source separation scan and a measured confining tension remain open.

criteria.title: Running coupling
criteria.requires: Resolve a coupling that changes with measurement scale, including the onset near the physical core radius.
criteria.note: A scale scan of a physical coupling referred to the same core radius remains open.

criteria.title: Weak force: muon decay
criteria.requires: Observe an identified muon decay into an electron with neutral products.
criteria.note: Muon, electron and neutral decay-product records remain open.

criteria.title: Weak force: beta decay (n → p)
criteria.requires: Resolve neutron decay into a proton, an electron and an antineutrino, and measure parity violation.
criteria.note: A tagged beta decay and its parity asymmetry remain open.

criteria.title: Gravity: Newton limit (GEM)
criteria.requires: Recover an attractive inverse-square force between masses from the gravitoelectromagnetic limit. Credit for the strength requires G to follow from the mechanism.
criteria.note: A sourced gravitoelectromagnetic force law and its strength remain unmeasured.

criteria.title: Gravity: local metric phenomena
criteria.requires: Measure local curved-metric phenomena with material clocks and light, such as bending, gravitational redshift or Shapiro delay.
criteria.note: A sourced gravitational field with independent clock or light propagation records remains open.

criteria.title: Cosmology: Λ / cosmic acceleration
criteria.requires: Obtain a cosmological constant that explains acceleration from the model dynamics, identify outstanding gaps and give a falsification test.
criteria.note: A derived cosmological constant, acceleration observable and falsification test remain open.

criteria.title: EM waves (Maxwell)
criteria.requires: Recover Maxwell dynamics and measure transverse electromagnetic disturbances travelling at the limiting speed.
criteria.note: The exports distinguish gapped propagating seam modes and a gapless scalar branch. The measured modes have yet to furnish Maxwell dynamics and a transverse electromagnetic signal at a common speed.

criteria.title: Quantum wave equation (Klein-Gordon)
criteria.requires: Recover the Klein–Gordon energy–momentum relation for propagating matter using independently identifiable spatial and temporal observables.
criteria.note: The measured one-cell scalar bands agree with the square of the first-order seam operator, ω² = m² + λ. A multi-cell matter wave with independently reconstructed physical momentum and the third spatial direction remains open.

criteria.title: Orbital quantization (atomic structure)
criteria.requires: Observe standing-wave bound levels with a hydrogen-like spectrum, including characteristic spacings.
criteria.note: Free scalar excitations have discrete cage levels. The quadratic matter sector supplies no hydrogen-like bound spectrum around another excitation.

requirements.title: Hypothetical gravitational particle
requirements.purpose: Track a quantum of the gravitational field alongside the Standard Model inventory. A classical spin-two wave and a quantum excitation receive distinct tests.

criteria.title: Graviton
criteria.requires: Tie a prepared or emitted neutral excitation to two transverse tidal polarizations on independent observers, a massless spin-two propagation law, universal coupling to stress and a positive quantum one-particle response on the same construction.
criteria.note: The candidate oscillator and cage preparations have no registered stress source and quantum tidal detector for this species.

requirements.title: Standard Model particle identifications
requirements.purpose: Identify all 17 elementary particle types on one frozen candidate. Each species has a local preparation or production channel, reproducible detection statistics, and a dictionary that distinguishes its nearest alternatives. A declaration of a field or an input mass cannot identify the excitation.
requirements.reference: Count six quark flavours, three charged leptons, three active neutrino flavour channels, four gauge-boson types and the Higgs. W covers both signs, and the gluon entry covers the eight colour components. Resolve conjugate partners where distinct. Neutrino flavour is defined by weak production and detection; its propagation can mix mass eigenstates. Composite hadrons provide evidence for confined quarks and gluons. The hypothetical graviton has its own gravitational-particle assessment. A sterile neutrino is outside this inventory.

criteria.note: No species assignment is registered.
